I'm from the midwest. Born in Michigan, lived in Wisconsin since I was 2 (visiting family in Michigan frequently).

I don't know about any jokes that are specific to my culture, we pretty much tell the same jokes you'd hear anywhere in the United States (and likely in most of the English-speaking world).

There are, however, many things considered normal in my culture that outsiders might call into question:

  • "Average" weight is about 20 lbs. heavier than in healthier areas of the world - and that's a generous estimate.
  • We drink a lot of beer, as I recently discovered when informed that anything over 5 drinks in one session is considered "binge drinking". In Wisconsin, 5 drinks is a typical night out for many people, myself included, and doesn't even necessarily result in intoxication if the drinking is well paced.
  • School/work isn't cancelled unless the weather drops to -30^o F or lower, and "snow" is not considered a viable excuse for being late. Everyone is pretty much expected to know how to drive on unpaved roads through 4 in. of unplowed snow in low visibility.
  • We eat cheese curds, which are essentially lumps of sour milk that are often deep fried.
  • This varies somewhat depending on where one lives in Wisconsin, but I've become so accustomed to the odor of cow shit that it's become a pleasant, nostalgic aroma to me.

If I meet my friends or parents on the street, I just say "hey" and stop to talk for a minute, even if I'm in a hurry. If I ever met my grandparents on the street, I imagine I'd be obliged to stop and talk even longer. If I met the president or the queen of England on the street, I probably wouldn't bother to greet them at all, but that's probably more of a personal choice than a cultural practice.
